slides.headline: Iran offers 7-day plan to reopen Hormuz
slides.body: Iran proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, with talks taking place through mediators.

photo.query: Strait of Hormuz satellite Wikimedia Commons
photo.prompt: wide aerial view of cargo ships near the Strait of Hormuz

slides.headline: That would reopen a key oil and gas route
slides.body: The strait provides the only sea passage from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean and carried 25% of seaborne oil trade and 20% of liquefied natural gas during 2023 to 2025.

photo.query: oil tanker Strait of Hormuz Wikimedia Commons
photo.prompt: oil tanker moving through a narrow gulf shipping lane at sunrise

slides.credit: Photo: Curt Teich & Co., Chicago (publisher / Public domain

slides.headline: And Iran says inspectors could return
slides.body: President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran would allow nuclear inspectors as part of the proposal.

photo.prompt: international nuclear inspection team entering a secure facility

slides.credit: Photo: Miami Beach Casino Co. / Public domain

slides.headline: But Trump reportedly rejected the proposal
slides.body: Trump reportedly rejected Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal tied to the seven-day Hormuz plan.

photo.prompt: the White House exterior at night with press lights outside

slides.headline: That leaves talks moving through mediators
slides.body: Iran offered the Hormuz reopening plan through Qatari mediators and awaited a U.S. response.

photo.prompt: Doha skyline with government buildings and flags

slides.headline: And the region is still under pressure
slides.body: Saudi coalition forces intercepted projectiles, while Pezeshkian said Iran no longer trusts talks with Washington.
